name: Emirati Samak Mashwi with Bezar and Basmati Rice

components.name: Samak Mashwi

ingredients.name: Raw boneless white fish fillets (instead of bone-in whole fish)

steps: Rub fish with bezar, garlic, lime juice, oil and salt, then refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 190 C and place fish in a baking dish over onion slices, with coriander on top; cover lightly with foil.
Bake 15-22 minutes depending on thickness until the centre of fish reaches 63 C; remove foil for the last few minutes if browning is desired.

components.name: Basmati Rice
steps: Cook dry basmati rice in measured water on the stove, then rest covered 10 minutes.

components.name: Carrot-Cucumber Side
steps: Pack the fish and onions with rice, and keep the crunchy raw carrot-cucumber-lemon side in a separate chilled container to add after reheating.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Emirati fish spice profile follows published Samak bil Fern. Boneless fillets and rice/salad are UNHANGRY batch adaptations.
Planning: SECONDARY STOVETOP: rice; fresh side packed separately.
Freezer: cooked fish and rice can freeze; fresh salad not suitable
Dietary: Contains fish; check bezar spice premix. Raw seafood never used for cold salad.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; freeze later-week portions soon after cooking.
Reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard. Use a food thermometer.
When a recipe includes rice, cool it rapidly and store cold immediately; avoid leaving cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Reheat crisp foods in oven when possible.
